title: Getting water; wells and windmills
description: Judith Jean McKinney explains how her family hauled and filtered water before a well existed, then how a well and windmill finally gave them a reliable supply at Black Rock.

title: Small farm house; enlarging it with the Black house
description: She describes the small homestead house on the Big Bend farm and how a former Black house was connected to the original house and painted white.

title: Medical help; having children at home
description: McKinney talks about doctors in nearby towns, giving birth at home, and who stayed with her to help after the babies were born.

title: Spokane house; Genesee and the Davies household
description: She recalls the Spokane house on 9th Street, the move to Genesee, Lottie Davies, and the people who helped care for young Kenny.

title: Show people; leather chair and pictures
description: The conversation turns to show people, a big leather rocking chair, pictures, and how furniture passed among family members.

title: Gardens, chickens, and milking
description: McKinney lists the farm work she did, such as gardening and tending chickens, and explains the times she did or did not milk cows.

title: Cream sales and butter
description: She describes milking seven or eight cows, keeping cream in the well, selling a five-gallon can daily, and making butter at home.

title: Sausage making and cottage cheese
description: She recalls her husband and helpers grinding and selling sausage, then explains her method for making cottage cheese and lye soap.

title: Butchering, canning meat, and boarding workers
description: McKinney talks about freezing and canning beef, feeding hired hands after haying, and a combine breaking down on the ranch.

title: Advice to young women
description: She tells advice she would give a young woman about whether she really wanted farm life and how it has changed with modern conveniences.

title: Magazines, television, and women's work
description: She names magazines she buys and discusses television shows she dislikes, along with her views on women's roles and army work.

title: Kerosene lamps; comparing old and new life
description: McKinney compares her earlier life of lamps and manual laundry with later electricity and remembers wheat decisions she discussed with her husband.
